text:
B: Hiya, you alright? Liam.
A: Hello, Liam. Tariq. Yes, fine, thank you.
B: Nice one. I have to say, mate, I clocked your picture earlier, navy quarter-zip. We've turned up in the same uniform.
A: So I see. I think it's the, er, the official dress code of people who have meetings about targets.
B: Ha, yeah, that's exactly it. Is that what you do then, targets?
A: Broadly. I'm a team leader at a contact centre in Stratford. Broadband and mobile, retentions mainly. People call to cancel, and we try to keep them.
B: Retentions, right. So you're basically talking people round. That's sales, to be fair.
A: It is, yes, though the company prefers the word "saving". I've got eleven advisers. And I keep my own spreadsheet of their numbers, because I like to know how the month looks before my manager does, you know.
B: No, I love that. I'm the same, my CRM is spotless, everyone takes the mick. I'm in technical sales, heating and air con, commercial. About sixty trade accounts round West Yorkshire. Top of the board at the minute, actually.
A: Congratulations. How long can you stay there?
B: That's the question, isn't it? It's March, everyone's chasing year end. But I'm going for area sales manager in the next couple of years, so I need to keep it up.
A: Same sort of position for me, operations manager. The trick, I think, is volunteering for the projects that the right people see. Not the ones that are useful. The ones that are visible, right?
B: Visible, yeah. That's proper advice, that. I'm writing that down.
A: Don't quote me to anyone senior.
B: Ha, I won't. Where are you based, London?
A: Ilford. Twenty-five years, roughly. Originally Karachi. And you?
B: Wakefield, born and bred. Do you get up north much?
A: Not often. I've been meaning to go to the Hepworth, actually. Barbara Hepworth, I like her work very much. And the building is supposed to be quite something.
B: The Hepworth! I've been, once, when family came over. It was alright. Bit odd, if I'm honest, lots of big holes in rocks. But the building's good, yeah, by the river.
A: Big holes in rocks is, er, not an unfair summary. That's partly the point. You walk round them and the shape changes. It's worth going slowly.
B: Fair enough, I'll give it another go. Do you follow football at all?
A: Cricket, mostly. Pakistan first, England second. I'll watch a full Test on catch-up, which my wife considers a medical condition.
B: Five days, mate! I can barely do ninety minutes of Leeds, and that's stressful enough. Do you do holidays, or is it all work?
A: I plan them in quite obsessive detail. Rome was the last proper one. A long weekend, but we upgraded the hotel, a terrace looking at the domes. Probably more than we should have spent.
B: Nah, that's what it's for though, isn't it? We did Dubai last year, rooftop pool, the lot. I've got a spreadsheet for every trip.
A: A spreadsheet. Then I think we'd get on.
B: Ha, definitely. Oh, that's the timer, I think.
A: It is. Good to meet you, Liam. Good luck with the board.
B: Cheers, Tariq, you too, mate.
